body:
Thanks for your contribution! I'm not sure this is a good idea because:

1. We already have `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE`. See [#105272](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105272) and [#105623](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105623).
2. The condition can't be too complex (only the name of another property). Or at least the condition must be a string, since annotation arguments must be constant expressions.
3. You can already use `_validate_property()` for this purpose. Yes, it requires `@tool`, but that's okay, since conditional exports are more of an advanced feature.

Also, if this feature is eventually approved, I don't think it should be a primary export annotation, but rather a modifier that could be combined with other export annotations, such as `@export_range`:

```gdscript
@export var is_alive := true

@export
@display_if("is_alive")
var is_friendly: bool

@export_range(0, 100, 1)
@display_if("is_alive")
var health: int
```

We already have two open PRs with similar modifier annotations:

* #101117
* #111636

But this is a new concept, and there's no consensus on it yet.

> We already have `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE`. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105272 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105623.

I don't see how this is relevant, it serves a completely different purpose, it only works for groups, not for individual properties.

> The condition can't be too complex (only the name of another property). Or at least the condition must be a string, since annotation arguments must be constant expressions.

I'm not quite sure what you mean by this. Could you clarify ?

> You can already use `_validate_property()` for this purpose. Yes, it requires `@tool`, but that's okay, since conditional exports are more of an advanced feature.

The proposal has 50 thumbs up and hiding or making certain properties read-only based on a condition is something i see asked quite often on forums and in discord. `_validate_property()` works sure, but it can quickly get big, especially in C# where it takes more lines to do than in GDScript. This would fix that with just a simple annotation.

> Also, if this feature is eventually approved, I don't think it should be a primary export annotation, but rather a modifier that could be combined with other export annotations, such as `@export_range`

Agreed, will make change. Note that this would then require a completely different attribute in C#, compared to the current implementation (although it is half-broken in C# for some reason)

I'm debating if there should be an extra argument that would only make it read-only instead of hidden completely ? I feel like that would also solve having to use _validate_property to make a property read-only, though maybe it would be better in a separation annotation entirely ? This was not mentioned in the original proposal but could be good to have.

> > We already have `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE`. See #105272 and #105623.
> 
> I don't see how this is relevant, it serves a completely different purpose, it only works for groups, not for individual properties.

Yes and no. You can use groups for simple (and most common) cases.

> > The condition can't be too complex (only the name of another property). Or at least the condition must be a string, since annotation arguments must be constant expressions.
> 
> I'm not quite sure what you mean by this. Could you clarify ?

I mean, how complex can the display conditions be? Do you or anyone else want complex conditions like:

```gdscript
@export @display_if("a and b") var c: int
@export @display_if("x > 0") var y: int
```

If so, then string conditions don't look very good due to the lack of validation and syntax highlighting, but we can't make them primary expressions because annotation arguments must be constant expressions (other kind of expressions are a completely new concept, currently missing from GDScript).

> The proposal has 50 thumbs up and hiding or making certain properties read-only based on a condition is something i see asked quite often on forums and in discord. `_validate_property()` works sure, but it can quickly get big, especially in C# where it takes more lines to do than in GDScript. This would fix that with just a simple annotation.

I don't dispute that this proposal has support. However, upvotes aren't the only or most important factor we should consider. Sometimes an idea looks cool and useful, but in reality, it's not as useful or often required as it might appear. We also need to keep in mind that this proposal was opened before `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE` was introduced.

We should consider other existing features and the flexibility they provide. `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE` is fairly simple, but limited.` _validate_property()` is quite versatile, but perhaps less convenient and requires `@tool`. The proposed feature falls somewhere in between, so it's a question of balancing simplicity and flexibility. If a new feature is too close to an existing feature and they both solve too similar problems, then its introduction is probably unjustified.

> PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE

Are there any examples in the docs on how to use it? I can't find any. Google search only shows me a link to the `GlobalScope` docs where there is a thousand different things and to the 4.5 update page on the Godot's primary website where there is a link to the implementation pull request without any examples (there is only one comment with the same question on how to even use it).

I think if there were any examples on how to actually use any of these hints there will be less confusion about them (because they can be handy in some situations).

> You can use groups for simple (and most common) cases.

`PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE` can work, however it requires `@export_group` and `@export_custom`, which would be annoying to use on, for example, a single property. I personally think `@display_if` would be better in that case.

> I mean, how complex can the display conditions be? 

Ah, I see, you can't do `@display_if("a and b")`, here's how it would be done instead:
```gdscript
var c := a and b
@export @display_if("c") var x: int

var d = x > 0
@export @display_if("d") var y: int
```
Being able to do `@display_if("a and b")` would require somehow parsing to the string to a bool, which would not only be very complicated but be more error-prone as it would be even easier than it already is to make a typo and for the annotation to break, which is why I landed on this implementation instead where should only put the name of a `bool` property. To make up for this, the documentation should state **very clearly** how to use it as it's probably not how most people will expect it to work, I'll start working on that.

> We also need to keep in mind that this proposal was opened before `PROPERTY_HINT_CONDITION` was introduced.

~~This PR introduces `PROPERTY_HINT_CONDITION`.~~ `PROPERTY_HINT_CONDITION` will be removed once `@export_if` becomes `@display_if`, because `@export_custom` and some other export annotations would override property hint.

> We should consider other existing features and the flexibility they provide. `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE` is fairly simple, but limited. `_validate_property()` is quite versatile, but perhaps less convenient and requires @tool. The proposed feature falls somewhere in between, so it's a question of balancing simplicity and flexibility. If a new feature is too close to an existing feature and they both solve too similar problems, then its introduction is probably unjustified.

I fully agree, however, I myself have come across many cases where I wanted to conditionally export a property, but often just gave up on exporting it because of `_validate_property()` and `_get_property_list()` and just printed it as a workaround. A `@display_if` annotation would get rid of needed `_validate_property()` to conditionally show/hide a property, making it more simple, and by allowing to use `@export` alongside it, makes it very flexible.

> > PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE > > Are there any examples in the docs on how to use it? ``` gdscript @export var character_name: String @export_group("Is Alive") @export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE, "") var is_alive: bool = true @export var is_friendly: bool @export_range(0, 100, 1) var health: int @export_group("Jump Enabled") @export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE, "") var jump_enabled: bool = true @export var jump_count: int = 1 @export var jump_speed: float = -100.0 ``` > > We also need to keep in mind that this proposal was opened before `PROPERTY_HINT_CONDITION` was introduced. > > ~This PR introduces `PROPERTY_HINT_CONDITION`~ I made a mistake with copy-paste, of course I meant `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE`. > > I mean, how complex can the display conditions be? > > Ah, I see, you can't do `@display_if("a and b")`, here's how it would be done instead: > > ```gdscript > var c := a and b > @export @display_if("c") var x: int > > var d = x > 0 > @export @display_if("d") var y: int > ``` If this supported more complex expressions, it would make more sense to me. With the current concept, where the `@display_if` argument can only point to another variable, mostly of `bool` type, this inevitably leads to comparisons with the `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE` feature. They are essentially the same except for the direction of the dependency. Yes, you need to use both `@export_group` (or `@export_subgroup`) and `@export_custom` to create a collapsible section, but you don't need to repeat any annotation for all the properties contained in that section. This is a less flexible but more hierarchical approach. Whereas the proposed `@display_if` allows for a slightly more flexible, but non-hierarchical and therefore less obvious behavior for the user. You can make properties depend on each other in any order, without any hierarchy. This raises questions about the order of property processing in the case of cyclic dependencies like: ```gdscript @export @display_if("b") var a: bool @export @display_if("a") var b: bool ``` > ```gdscript > var c := a and b > @export @display_if("c") var x: int > ``` I don't think this will work since export variables are assigned after initialization. But even if you fix this example (probably with a getter of `c`), it's still not a clean and complete solution. It's an unintuitive boilerplate and possibly unnecessary intermediate variable. Which, in my opinion, is worse than the need for `@export_group` plus `@export_custom` in the case with `PROPERTY_HINT_GROUP_ENABLE`.

You're right, as much as I wanted this to work, there are too many hiccups for this to ever be usable in GDScript. It could maybe work in C# as it allows for an actual argument of type `bool` in attributes , but I'm not sure if that's a good idea as it'll cause more feature disparity, I'd have to leave a comment in the proposal to see if this is wanted (although i doubt it).

I have pushed my changes to rename the annotation to `@display_if`, just in case. I will now close the PR.
